content: Thunderbird has been evolving for decades and will continue in that direction. It isn't just to be innovative; Thunderbird needs to change over time to support new directions by email providers and evolving protocols. This is everywhere; if you monitor email clients, then you are aware that both Mailbird and eM Client have just initiated their own new directions and expansion. Change happens everywhere. Businesses that use software as part of the business's workflow should go slowly when upgrading the software, whether it is Quickbooks or Thunderbird or other. Businesses need also to do routine backups, as glitches do happen, whether software or hardware. I might add that this forum is staffed by volunteers; we do not design the changes, nor do we write the code. We are users, the same as you. I share your concerns, but I believe our best strategy is to stay the course; Thunderbird keeps getting better, and coping with a bump here and there seems preferable to changing to a new course. There are just my personal comments. Was there a specific new feature that is your concern? Thank you.

content:
- Who is your email provider?

- What anti-virus/network security/VPN software do you use, if any?

Certificate errors can be caused by several things, including:

- Wrong server settings. You should confirm that they are correct. The settings are usually found on the provider's web site, or you may need to contact them

- A-V software can interfere with secure connection. Norton and McAfee are especially notorious for this. You can disable them or create an exception for Thunderbird or turn off all email scanning features to test. If you use Windows you can restart in Safe Mode with Networking to test.

- Your provider may truly be having server or certificate problems. Only they can fix this. You can contact them to report the problem (they may already be aware) and to find out the status.
